item.title: Describing trends
item.description: Language for describing change in charts, data and reports.

children.example: There was a surge in online orders during the holidays.

children.definition: to fall very quickly and suddenly
to keep changing, going up and down
children.example: The price of fruit fluctuates throughout the year.

children.definition: developing gradually and evenly, without sudden changes
children.example: The company has seen steady growth over the past five years.

children.definition: to reach the highest point or level
children.example: Electricity use peaks in July, when everyone switches on the air conditioning.

children.definition: to stop rising or falling and stay at the same level
children.example: After years of growth, sales have levelled off.

children.definition: a gradual decrease in amount, quality or importance
children.example: A decline in readers forced the magazine to close.
The difference between the two prices is marginal.

children.definition: sudden and very large or noticeable
children.example: The new metro line led to a dramatic fall in journey times.

children.definition: to become twice as big or twice as many
children.example: The number of users doubled in just six months.

children.definition: to be more in number than another group
children.example: On this course, women outnumber men by three to one.

children.definition: to form a particular part or amount of a total
children.example: Rent accounts for almost half of my monthly spending.
